claims: LIDAR Composite DTM 1m is a raster terrain model covering about 99 percent of England.
Surface objects are removed from the DSM to produce terrain-only DTM values.
Newest best-resolution repeat survey data is used and resampled areas use bilinear interpolation.
The dataset CRS is EPSG:27700 and stated vertical accuracy is plus or minus 15cm RMSE.
Metadata survey indexes identify which survey contributes at a location.
WCS, WMS, WMTS and OGC API services are listed, but candidate numeric extraction requires exact coverage bytes.
Open-standard WCS and WMS replace retired Esri image services.
WMS is a summarised visualisation while WCS provides elevation coverage.
Persistent service names were introduced so current composite endpoints can update without annual URL changes.
Time-stamped DTM tiles are delivered as GeoTIFF rasters in 5km zip files.
Values are metres referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn and aligned to the OS Grid.
Metadata records survey dates, resolution, transformation and geoidal model.
All LIDAR data is stated as plus or minus 15cm RMSE.

quality_guards: Use DTM rather than DSM for ground-height difference.
Treat RMSE, resampling and survey age as uncertainty, not as exact candidate height.
Require exact TQ2892 filtered metadata and WCS raster values before numeric promotion.
Do not substitute WMS colour or hillshade pixels for elevation samples.
